chapter: Postwar: Chicago, Vinson, Hines and Cootie
title: His first record session, with McShann in Dallas
summary: His first record date was with McShann for Dave Kapp in Dallas, including 'Confessing the Blues' with Charlie Parker.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Now, that's something we haven't talked about yet. When did you make your first record session?
My very first record session was with MacShann, I believe it was.
Oh, before you went in the Army and before he went in the Army.
Well, was Walter Brown with him?
So it was that date, wasn't it?
Our first date was in Dallas, Texas.
And the other blues. " Hootie " Hoodie Blues.
Yeah. Were you kind of thrilled with that, the fact that you were recording?
No, it didn't bother me. Charlie Parker was with us on that.
Yeah, that's right. That's when he showed what he sounded like when he played.
And we made that in Dallas, Texas.
Yeah, so you didn't tighten up or the band didn't tighten up when you were recording, like some people do.
You had also rehearsed, didn't you?
Well, I guess maybe some of the guys could have been kind of uptight.
For their first record date, too.
We were trying to be perfect, anyway, with it.
I mean, all those takes. It gets you down a little at times, doesn't it. You begin to wonder if you (unintelligible).
Yes, but we didn't have that many mikes, you know.
They'd put one mike up there.
And then the drums, they were always soft -- putting you down, weren't they?
It was always coming through too heavy in those days, wasn't it?
It has to bother a drummer, doesn't it?
Oh, yeah, you're afraid to play anything.
Yeah, hold back, hold back all the time.
Oh, I guess I felt a little bit --
Well, that was your first session.
